responses.content:
There is no credible evidence to suggest that Albert Einstein failed math in school. In fact, Einstein was known for his academic abilities and excelled in mathematics from an early age. He attended the Swiss Federal Polytechnic University, where he studied physics and mathematics, and graduated with a degree in 1900.

Einstein's math skills were so advanced that he was able to teach himself advanced calculus and differential equations, which he would later use to develop his theory of relativity. His understanding of mathematical concepts, including geometry, algebra, and number theory, was highly developed and helped him to make significant contributions to physics.

It's worth noting that Einstein's academic performance was not unusually high, and he did not have a particularly strong record in math. However, he was able to apply his knowledge of mathematics to develop new ideas and theories that revolutionized our understanding of the universe.
